audit.summary: The asserted support-narrowing-to-entropy implication fails while value and feasibility remain optimal. The released automatic tree selector omits ancestor factors and chooses a different strategy on an actual supplied tree. Shared evaluation/training environment creates a separate local rollout defect. Appendix A finite-policy proofs withstand the described checks; historical empirical impact remains unresolved.
limitations: Narrowing a policy support does not guarantee lower Shannon entropy — Counterevidence: Uniform distributions on finite supports would give monotonic log-cardinality; not imposed. The inequality could be a desired assumption, but hierarchy alone does not enforce it. Paper explicitly disclaims application of PAC theorem to implemented learner; AppendixA remains valid.

Released strategy selector uses local rather than root-relative priority — Counterevidence: Reflected easy tree and medium variants have same argmax under both formulas. CLI explicit node/branch selection can bypass automatic choice. Historical experiment commit and ranking stages unverified. Root-relative fields would be a different representation inconsistent with current parent-relative value semantics.

Evaluation mutates the training environment while PPO retains stale observations — Counterevidence: No actual Crafter/author program executed; both baseline and guided use wrapper. Frequency/material comparative effect in historical experiments not established. No inference of bias direction.
Unresolved item: Section5.2 top-two selection versus medium Tables9-10 Craft/Hunt/Breed ranking and main Hunt/Breed comparisons; Figure3/reflection stages may explain, but exact run records absent.
Unresolved item: Reward model uses pretrained PPO/expert frames. Downstream online curves do not account for checkpoint creation and data collection/amortization.
Unresolved item: Raw seed-level curves, checkpoints, exact run configs, EDE/Dreamer experimental source and historical commit not established.

proposition.claim:
Section4.3 asserts by-design child entropy lower than parent; AppendixB.2.1 says hierarchical narrowing implicitly lowers entropy despite no explicit entropy calculation.

AppendixB.2 selects max product of root-relative feasibility and value, each accumulated over the root-to-candidate path.

Paper describes ordinary PPO training with periodic evaluation; released train() passes same environment object to evaluation callback.
proposition.domain: Completed report for I25-43567; exact inspected scope and limitations are retained in the report and coverage ledger.
assumptions: One-step finite MDP, three deterministic actions/policies, each reward1 and then termination, gamma0.9
Parent masses(.98,.01,.01); child is exact parent conditional distribution on policies1,2
Proper subset support, normalized finite distributions, all policies implementable
Hmax0.2, tau0.005, vmin0.1; both relative and additive near-optimality requirements satisfied
Sequential nodes treated as terminal candidates as in released selector
Exact supplied easy tree.json values, no tie
Training and evaluation share same underlying environment object as released assignment eval_env=self.env
Evaluation callback resets and steps it before training collection resumes
No environment-state restoration or observation synchronization

repair.content:
Explicitly constrain and enforce distributions, e.g. uniform finite supports, or withdraw the automatic entropy guarantee and identify specificity as a heuristic.

Accumulate ancestor feasibility/value factors for every candidate path (or explicitly store correctly converted root-relative quantities).

Use an independent evaluation environment and seed/wrapper configuration.
